findings.subject: HEADLINE CORRECTION — the 13 'cross-customer' billing rows J3 cites are not cross-customer
findings.measurement: billing_line_items = 173 rows. 72 have a non-empty customer_name. 13 of those 72 differ from their booking's customer_name by exact string. After normalisation (upper + strip non-alphanumeric), HARD mismatches = 0 of 72. All 13 sit on ONE booking (15ab53ca-b825-40d0-94e7-1846dbbb6a38 / BR202606-073) and are the single pair 'Garden Barn Inc.' vs 'GARDEN BARN INC'. Examples: BIL-1780890866622-t47k2twa, BIL-1780970539809-yayj1j06, BIL-1780973999352-c1fmq9vw.

Literally true, semantically misleading: it is a casing/punctuation difference on one customer, not money on the wrong tenant. There are ZERO hard cross-customer rows in billing_line_items on dev today.

findings.subject: Cross-parent customer disagreement across the whole money graph
findings.measurement: billing_line_items -> booking (normalised customer_name): 0 of 72. billing_line_items -> evoucher (booking_id equality): 0 of 97. billing_line_items -> invoice (booking_id equality): 0 of 13. billing_line_items -> invoice (normalised customer_name vs booking): 0 of 13. invoices -> booking (customer_id): 0 of 9; (normalised customer_name): 0 of 13. collections -> invoice (customer_id): 0 of 6; (customer_name): 0 of 6. evoucher_line_items -> evoucher (booking_id, both non-null): 0 of 254. bookings -> customers (normalised name): 0 of 235. bookings -> projects (customer_id): 0 of 10.
findings.interpretation: BY DESIGN-adjacent good news. Not one hard cross-tenant link exists in live dev data. A same-customer constraint expressed on the FK'd columns would reject ZERO existing rows. J3's structural claim (nothing enforces it) is confirmed; its data claim (it has already happened) is not.

findings.subject: billing_line_items.project_number is a wrong-namespace string, not a project reference
findings.measurement: 173 rows: 87 are the empty string '', 0 are NULL, 86 are non-empty. Of the 86, 83 fail to resolve against projects.project_number, and all 83 are exactly the booking_number of their own booking_id. The 3 that DO resolve (PRJ-899414, PRJ-550146, PRJ-291528) all point at a project whose customer_id matches the booking's — 0 mismatches. Same shape on evouchers: 249 of 264 have a non-empty project_number, 0 resolve to projects.project_number, 244 equal their own booking's booking_number, and 0 disagree with their own booking's number.
findings.interpretation: PATTERN, and it is a naming bug rather than a tenancy breach. The column holds booking numbers under a project-shaped name. A 'project_number must resolve to projects' CHECK would reject 83 of 173 billing rows and 249 of 264 e-vouchers. The correct fix is renaming/relocating the column, not constraining it.

findings.subject: Writer attribution on billing_line_items — the dominant writer is exactly the one that omits tenancy
findings.measurement: 97 of 173 rows carry evoucher_id (written by ensure_billable_expense_billing_item; confirmed by reading pg_get_functiondef — it inserts id, booking_id, project_number, evoucher_id, source_*, description, service_type, amount, currency, status, category and NOTHING else). findings.subject: Money with no resolvable tenancy at all (orphans)

findings.subject: bookings is a clean root of truth — the join every rule must be expressed against
findings.measurement: 240 rows. customer_id populated 235, dangling 0, normalised customer_name vs customers.name mismatches 0. The 5 NULL customer_id rows are 4 KPI simulation fixtures (SIM-BK01..04) plus one cancelled booking with an empty customer_name (BRK-2026-0041); all 5 have 0 billing rows and 0 e-vouchers. project_id populated on only 10 of 240 (the recon said 9 of 239; one booking was added since). Every one of the 173 billing rows resolves to a booking that HAS a customer_id — 173 of 173.
findings.interpretation: BY DESIGN. Tenancy is derivable for 100% of billing rows and 244 of 264 e-vouchers by walking booking_id -> bookings.customer_id. That makes a booking-keyed constraint cheap and a customer_name-keyed one expensive.

findings.subject: Nothing anywhere enforces tenancy — confirmed at both layers
findings.measurement: Across billing_line_items, invoices, collections, evouchers, evoucher_line_items and expenses: 30 RLS policies total, 0 whose USING or WITH CHECK expression mentions customer / project_number / booking. CHECK constraints on those tables number 2 in total (billing_line_items_amount_nonnegative, evoucher_line_items_fault_class_check) and neither is tenancy-related. Additionally EVERY money-graph FK is ON DELETE SET NULL: billing_line_items.booking_id/project_id/invoice_id/evoucher_id, evouchers.booking_id/project_id/customer_id, invoices.booking_id/customer_id/project_id/evoucher_id, collections.*. The only CASCADE is evoucher_line_items.evoucher_id.
findings.interpretation: BY DESIGN (structural), and worse than stated. ON DELETE SET NULL means deleting a booking silently converts its billing lines and e-vouchers into untenanted money rather than refusing. The schema does not merely fail to prevent orphans, it manufactures them.

findings.subject: Tables the recon listed or missed, by row count
findings.measurement: billing_line_items 173, evouchers 264, evoucher_line_items 274, invoices 13, collections 6, bookings 240, projects 15, customers 147, quotations 312. findings.subject: Consequence of the header-booking regression on the billable-expense trigger — flagged, unproven

Since 2026-07-28 all 7 new e-vouchers have NULL booking_id. But the most recent e-voucher with details->>'is_billable' = 'true' was EV-2026-0257, created 2026-07-15, booking_id populated, and it DID mint its billing row (1 row). If the current form still writes header booking_id NULL, a billable expense will mint no receivable and the revenue is silently lost — but no live row exercises it, so I am reporting the mechanism, not a confirmed leak.

findings.subject: Catalog doctrine (G5) counted while I was in the tables — context for sequencing
findings.measurement: billing_line_items.catalog_item_id NULL on 125 of 173 (of which 97 are the trigger's, which never sets it). evoucher_line_items.catalog_item_id NULL on 72 of 274.
findings.interpretation: PATTERN. Not tenancy, but it shares the blocker: the same dominant writer defeats both the catalog CHECK and any customer_name rule. Whoever fixes the trigger should fix both in one pass rather than backfilling twice.

proposals.rule: NOT NULL — every revenue line must name a booking. This is the tenancy key that is actually reliable (the FK'd one), and it is the join every other rule should be expressed through rather than through denormalised strings.

proposals.target: billing_line_items.booking_id / evouchers.booking_id / invoices.booking_id / collections.booking_id — FK ON DELETE
proposals.rule: Change ON DELETE SET NULL to ON DELETE RESTRICT on the money-graph booking/customer/invoice edges. Today deleting a booking silently converts its revenue lines and e-vouchers into untenanted money; the schema manufactures the very violation J3 wants to forbid. Zero rows are affected because this constrains future deletes, not existing data.
Trigger: a line's booking_id, when non-null, must equal its parent e-voucher's booking_id. Zero of the 254 rows where both are populated violate this.
Trigger: a collection's customer must equal the customer on the invoice it settles. All 6 rows already comply. WARNING: this is a 6-row sample — the rule is right but the evidence is thin.

Trigger: an invoice's customer must equal its booking's customer, compared on customer_id where present and on a NORMALISED name (upper, strip non-alphanumeric) otherwise. All 13 rows already comply on both axes.

Trigger: when non-empty, must NORMALISE-equal the booking's customer_name. Zero hard violations. If written as an EXACT string comparison instead, it rejects 13 rows (all on booking BR202606-073, 'Garden Barn Inc.' vs 'GARDEN BARN INC') — so the normalisation is what makes this free. Better still: stop denormalising and derive the name from the booking, since 101 of 173 rows have it NULL anyway.

Add a real FK'd customer_id and backfill it from bookings.customer_id. Every one of the 173 billing rows resolves to a booking that has a customer_id, so the backfill is 100% mechanical and total. This replaces the unreliable customer_name string with the boundary J3 actually wants, and it is what a same-customer CHECK should key on.

NOT NULL. DO NOT DO THIS YET — 20 of 264 rows fail, and critically 7 of the 7 e-vouchers created since 2026-07-28 fail, i.e. 100% of what the product writes today. Fix the writer first (it moved the booking link from the header to the line items), backfill the 6 headers whose own line items already name a booking, then decide individually about the 14 remaining — including EV-2026-0001, which is disbursed cash against a reference that resolves to nothing.

Backfill from invoices.booking_id (all 6 collections have a resolvable invoice, all 6 invoices have a booking_id), then constrain to equal the settled invoice's booking. Cash is currently linked to a customer string and to an invoice, and not to the booking at all.

Do NOT add a resolves-to-projects CHECK. The column does not hold project numbers: 83 of 86 non-empty billing values and 249 of 249 e-voucher values are BOOKING numbers, and each equals its own booking's number (0 internal disagreements). Rename the column to booking_number_snapshot, or drop it and derive from booking_id. A resolves-to-projects constraint would reject 83 billing rows and 249 e-vouchers — an outage, not a fix. Also normalise the 87 empty strings on billing_line_items to NULL as part of the same migration.

Make the trigger set customer_id (and catalog_item_id) from the booking it already reads, instead of copying evouchers.project_number verbatim. It wrote 97 of 173 billing rows with customer_name NULL, catalog_item_id NULL and 83 wrong-namespace project_numbers — it is the single writer standing between the data and every rule above. It also returns early with 'no_booking_id', which means under the current e-voucher writer (header booking_id NULL on all 7 recent rows) a billable expense may mint no receivable at all. Verify that before shipping any tenancy migration.

blockers: The samples for invoices (13 rows) and collections (6 rows) are too small to call anything proven. Zero violations across 13 and 6 rows is consistent with a real invariant and equally consistent with nobody having exercised the path. Treat the invoice and collection rules as low-risk-to-apply but not as evidence that the code is correct.

expenses, transactions, budget_requests, project_bookings and contract_bookings are all EMPTY on dev (0 rows). Their tenancy is UNANSWERABLE — I measured nothing about them and no count from them should be quoted. expenses in particular carries the full FK set (booking_id, project_id, evoucher_id, catalog_item_id) and is entirely unused.

Multi-booking invoices are UNEXERCISED: 0 of 13 invoices have more than one entry in booking_ids. The cross-customer multi-booking case — the obvious way to smuggle two tenants onto one invoice — cannot be measured on live data. Any rule about booking_ids is being written without evidence.
collections.customer_id_alt is populated on 0 of 6 rows, so I could not determine from data which of customer_id / customer_id_alt the app writes. That needs a code read, not a query.

Whether the current e-voucher form still leaves header booking_id NULL is a code question I did not answer. It matters more than anything else in this survey: it determines whether proposal 8 is a backfill of 20 historical rows or an ongoing bleed, and whether billable expenses are currently minting receivables at all.

This survey measured DISAGREEMENT between populated tenancy fields. It did not and could not measure whether a populated field is CORRECT — e.g. a billing line whose booking_id points at the wrong customer's booking entirely would read as perfectly consistent here, because every denormalised field is copied from that same wrong booking. Consistency is not correctness; only the booking is a root of truth, and nothing audits the bookings themselves.
survey.notes:
The short version for whoever writes the migration.

The constraint J3 asks for is CHEAPER than J3 implies, and the reason is that J3's one piece of data evidence does not survive inspection. The "13 billing rows whose customer_name disagrees with their booking" are 13 rows on ONE booking for ONE customer, differing by "Garden Barn Inc." vs "GARDEN BARN INC". Normalise the string and the count is zero. Across the entire money graph — 173 billing lines, 264 e-vouchers, 274 e-voucher lines, 13 invoices, 6 collections, 240 bookings — there is not one hard cross-customer link on dev today. A same-customer rule keyed on booking_id would reject nothing.

What actually blocks a strict constraint is not corruption, it is two naming/population problems:

  1. project_number is not a project number. On billing_line_items 83 of 86 non-empty values are booking numbers; on evouchers it is 249 of 249. Every one of them equals its OWN booking's number, so the data is internally consistent — it is the column name that lies. A resolves-to-projects CHECK is an outage (332 rows), a rename is free.

  2. evouchers.booking_id has gone dark in the current code path. 20 of 264 are NULL overall, but 7 of the 7 e-vouchers created since 2026-07-28 are NULL, and the last one with a booking_id was 2026-07-18. The link moved to the line items (6 line items now carry a booking_id their parent header does not). So the single most obvious rule — "an e-voucher must name a booking" — would today reject 100% of what the product writes. That is exactly the failure mode the task warned about, and it is a live regression, not legacy debt.

The dominant-writer risk the recon flagged is real and I confirmed its shape by reading the function. ensure_billable_expense_billing_item wrote 97 of 173 billing rows; it sets booking_id and project_number and nothing else — customer_name NULL on all 97, catalog_item_id NULL on all 97, and it is the sole source of all 83 wrong-namespace project_numbers. Any rule keyed on customer_name or catalog_item_id breaks it; any rule keyed on booking_id does not touch it, because it copies booking_id verbatim off the parent voucher and therefore cannot mismatch. That is the whole argument for expressing tenancy through booking_id and deriving everything else.

One thing nobody has written down: every FK in the money graph is ON DELETE SET NULL. Delete a booking and its revenue lines, e-vouchers and invoices quietly become untenanted money rather than the delete being refused. The schema does not merely fail to prevent the violation J3 describes — it has a button that creates it. RESTRICT on those edges costs zero rows and should go in the same migration as anything else.

Order I would ship: (1) fix the e-voucher writer so booking_id lands on the header again, and confirm whether billable expenses are still minting receivables — the trigger returns early on a NULL booking_id, so they may not be. (2) Ship the zero-backfill rules: billing_line_items.booking_id NOT NULL, FK RESTRICT, line-vs-parent booking equality, collection-vs-invoice customer, invoice-vs-booking customer. (3) Add and backfill billing_line_items.customer_id from the booking — 173 of 173 resolve, it is fully mechanical, and it gives the constraint a real key instead of a string. (4) Rename project_number. (5) Only then revisit e-voucher booking_id NOT NULL, and handle the 5 orphan vouchers — one of them, EV-2026-0001, is disbursed cash against a reference that resolves to nothing — as individual human decisions rather than a backfill.

Harness rules: K1 did not bite here (this was a service-role survey, so denied-SELECT-returns-empty was not in play), but K1's cousin was everywhere — an empty table reads exactly like a clean table. expenses, transactions and budget_requests all have 0 rows and I have reported them as UNANSWERABLE rather than counting them as clean, and the same caution applies to the 13-row invoices and 6-row collections samples.

attack.notes:
SCOPE. Probe 1 (send_billing_items_to_booking cross-customer via the NULL project_id skip) was NOT re-attacked as an open hole — as instructed it was re-verified and is STILL CLOSED (BLOCKED_LOUD, with the same-customer positive control still passing). The six worked probes are ranks 2-7 from phase1-spec.json -> fks.probes; rank 7 was run twice (Ops TL and the Executive ceiling) and each half of it (project re-parent, customer rename) counted separately, which is why 9 breaches come out of 6 ranked probes.

HEADLINE. Every cross-tenant write attempted landed. Not one raised, not one was silently filtered. Nine for nine. J3's structural claim is now empirically confirmed, not inferred: the database enforces tenancy nowhere on the money graph — not by RLS, not by CHECK, not by trigger, not by FK.

METHOD, against K1/K2/K3.
- K3: all three actors (treasury@, jr.supervisor07@, inquiry@) were signed in and their auth uid captured BEFORE any probe; the driver throws on a failed sign-in rather than proceeding. Re-verified independently afterwards — treasury uid b203e835…, supervisor07 uid 3b72a9b7…, inquiry uid 29e857a0…. No login failed, so no verdict here rests on a dead password.
- K1: no verdict was taken from the absence of an error. Every probe read the row back with the service-role client and compared the actual stored value. BREACH means service-role SAW the change.
- K2: every write targeted a value the row did not already hold. P5's invoice_id was NULL before being pointed at customer B's invoice; P7a moved project_id from A's project to B's; P7b changed customer_name from 'E2E-TENANCY CUSTOMER A'. No from === to probes. The P7 pair was restored between the Ops and Executive runs so the Executive attempt was also a genuine change, not a no-op reading as success.

THE TWO RESULTS THAT ARE WORSE THAN THE RANKING SUGGESTS.
1. P3 is the one that propagates. The Ops TL — who holds no billings grant — inserted one e-voucher against another customer's booking with is_billable true, and trg_ensure_billable_expense_billing_on_approval minted a 50,000 customer-facing receivable on that foreign booking by itself, through a SECURITY DEFINER function, with customer_name NULL and catalog_item_id NULL. One AP write on the wrong booking becomes revenue on the wrong client with no second actor involved. Note this trigger fires on INSERT as well as UPDATE, and status was set directly in the insert — the 270/273 status guard is a BEFORE UPDATE trigger and does not see a row created at pending_accounting.
2. P7 breached identically for the Ops team leader and for the Executive account that holds 'everything' on all 21 record types. When the ceiling and the floor get the same answer, the absence is structural. Re-parenting is also the lever that decides whether the J1 guard can resolve a tenancy relationship at all — anyone who can move a booking's project_id or rewrite its customer_name can change what the one guard that DOES work is comparing.

WHAT I DID NOT DETERMINE.
- Whether these writes are reachable through the app's own UI. The probes deliberately went at PostgREST with the anon key plus a real session, which is what a browser console, a stale tab or a copied bearer token has. 'The form does not offer it' remains untested and is a different claim.

proposals.rule: invoice_transition(p_invoice_id, p_to_status, p_reason) SECURITY DEFINER + BEFORE UPDATE guard on the column, modelled verbatim on 270. Edges: (INSERT)->'draft' requires current_user_can_invoices('create'); 'draft'->'posted' requires current_user_can_invoices('edit') AND the row's approval_status='approved' (move the InvoiceBuilder.tsx:1015 client check server-side, and drop the `?? 'void','reversed','reversal_posted' are terminal — no outbound edges. Reject 'issued','voided','paid','overdue' outright: no writer produces them. Service-role bypass when auth.uid() IS NULL, as in 270.

Forbid ALL direct writes to approval_status via a BEFORE UPDATE trigger; approve_invoice() is the sole door (it already re-checks is_invoice_approver_of and RAISEs). Single edge: 'pending_approval'->'approved' by the materialized approver. Additionally ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT 'pending_approval' — today's default 'approved' means any INSERT that omits the column lands pre-approved, which defeats NEU-103 without touching the status column at all. Add a rejection edge only if the product grows one; none exists today (0 live rows are pending).

collection_transition() + BEFORE UPDATE guard. Edges: (INSERT)->'posted' requires current_user_can_collections('create'); 'posted'->'credited' and 'posted'->'refunded' require current_user_can_collections('edit') (collectionResolution.ts:63 already pairs each with an evoucher_transition call, so the two machines stay in step). 'credited' and 'refunded' are terminal. Reject 'cleared' and 'deposited' — dead literals. Also change the column default from 'pending' to 'posted', or add 'pending' as a legal insert state; today the default is a value the product never produces and the matrix would have no from-edge for.

Guard must cover INSERT as well as UPDATE — two SECURITY DEFINER functions insert rows and a BEFORE UPDATE trigger will never see them. On INSERT: status must be 'unbilled' (pin it in send_billing_items_to_booking rather than reading it from p_items — that payload is caller-controlled). On UPDATE: 'unbilled'->'invoiced' requires current_user_can_invoices('edit') AND invoice_id IS NOT NULL in the same statement; 'invoiced'->'unbilled' requires invoices:edit or invoices:delete AND invoice_id set to NULL in the same statement (the two release paths, InvoiceBuilder.tsx:1078 and :1148, both already do this); 'unbilled'->'voided' requires current_user_can_billings('edit') AND invoice_id IS NULL. No 'invoiced'->'voided' edge — void the invoice first. 'voided' is terminal. NOTE: billing_line_items_update's USING clause calls current_user_can_view_record('billings', NULL) — the E15/G3/G7 NULL-owner bug — so the grant side of this is broken independently of the matrix.

BEFORE UPDATE guard alongside the existing CHECK (the CHECK constrains the value, not the edge). Edges: 'unbilled'->'billed' requires current_user_can_invoices('edit') (today's only writer, workflowTickets.ts:221, runs on ticket resolution behind a client-side canExecuteResolutionAction); 'unbilled'->'partial' and 'partial'->'billed' same authority — but note NOTHING writes 'partial' today, so either add the writer or drop the value from the CHECK; 'billed'->'unbilled' requires invoices:delete — this edge does not exist in code and SHOULD: voiding an invoice releases the line items but leaves the booking flagged billed.

booking_transition() + BEFORE UPDATE guard. Three layers. (a) Value: must be in SERVICE_STATUS_OPTIONS[service_type] UNION {'Created'} — 'Created' is written on insert and offered by no selector, so it must be admitted explicitly or 128 of 240 rows strand. (b) The cancel edge, lifted server-side from src/utils/bookingCancellation.ts: ->'Cancelled' requires from IN ('Created','Draft','Pending','Confirmed','In Progress','On Hold') AND zero linked rows in invoices, collections, expenses, evouchers (booking_id = id OR booking_ids @> array[id]). Same trigger as quotations.status, separate branch. survey.notes:
METHOD. Everything measured against dev (oqermaidggvanahumjmj) by read-only SELECT: distinct status values WITH counts for all 15 columns in one query, pg_constraint contype='c' over 13 tables, pg_trigger (29 non-internal triggers), information_schema.columns for defaults, pg_policies for UPDATE/ALL, and pg_proc.prosrc for guard_user_privileged_columns, approve_invoice, ensure_billable_expense_billing_item and repoint_live_bookings_to_rate_version. No writes. supabase-prod never touched. Code side: grepped src/ for every .from(<table>).update/.insert touching a status column and read each call site in context for its gate.

WHAT THE RECON GOT WRONG, VERIFIED. Three corrections. (1) projects.status — recon says "no app-side status write found"; there are two, ProjectDetail.tsx:305 and the cross-module cascade at QuotationFileView.tsx:626, and a real ProjectStatus union of 4 values, not 1. (2) users.status — recon's open question 7 asked whether trg_guard_user_privileged_columns protects it. It does not; the function's distinct-from list is access_profile_id, role, department, team_id, is_active. Status is the unprotected twin of is_active, and the self-update policy (auth_id = auth.uid()) makes it self-writable. (3) bookings live count is 240 not 239, and Created is 128 not 127 — one booking was added since the recon.

WHAT THE RECON GOT RIGHT, CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY. evouchers is the only guarded status column (29 triggers enumerated, none status-aware). Exactly one status CHECK among the 15 (bookings.billing_status). No InvoiceStatus and no CollectionStatus TS union exists — the recon's codeValues for those two are harvested literals and must not be treated as declared vocabularies. 'Issued' (4 invoices) and 'Approved' (1 evoucher) are the two capitalised-legacy residues.

THE SHAPE THAT REPEATS ACROSS ALL FIFTEEN. Every write site is `.update({status: X})` with X chosen by a dropdown and the authority check living in a React `if`. The only from-state logic anywhere in src/ is bookingCancellation.ts, and it runs in the browser. The database is asked WHO you are (via the RLS grant helpers) and never WHERE the record is — the exact sentence migration 270 was written to falsify for one table.

THE SECOND-ORDER PROBLEM, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN SOME OF THE MATRICES. Two policies make a transition guard beside the point. projects_update has WITH CHECK = true and a USING clause satisfied by any of four VIEW grants: a view-grant holder rewrites every column of a project. transactions_update has the same shape (WITH CHECK true, view-only USING) and is only harmless because the table is empty. Guarding projects.status while leaving that policy is 270's own lesson repeated — the lock on the door beside the open window.

ORDER OF WORK I'D RECOMMEND. Ranks 1-4 (invoices.status, invoices.approval_status, collections.status, billing_line_items.status) are one migration: they are the money chain, their matrices are small and fully derived from real writers, and three of the four have zero backfill. Rank 2 is the cheapest real win in the whole survey — it is one ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT plus a trigger that forbids direct writes, and it closes three independent bypasses of the same approval. Ranks 5-9 are a second migration and need the stranded-row queries run against prod first (bookings.status strands 128 dev rows unless 'Created' is admitted explicitly). Rank 10 (users.status) is a two-line addition to an existing trigger and should ride along with whichever migration ships first. Ranks 11-12 are cosmetic; write them only if the fifteen-column completeness matters more than the churn on every customer and task save. Ranks 13-15 should not ship as guards at all — for transactions, ship the policy fix instead.

TWO THINGS EVERY MIGRATION MUST CARRY, from 270's own header. First, the `if auth.uid() is not null` bypass, or the clone script (scripts/clone-prod-to-dev.mjs, service-role, truncate-and-rewrite) and the admin-user-actions Edge Function both break. Second, an OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status entry condition — customers, tasks and quotations are all written by whole-row updates, and without it every ordinary save is a transition attempt. This is also K2 in trigger form: a write that sets a column to the value it already holds must be a no-op, not an edge.

STRANDED-ROW QUERY TO RUN BEFORE EACH MIGRATION. For each target: SELECT status, count(*) FROM <table> WHERE status NOT IN (<every value that appears as a `from` OR a `to` in the proposed matrix>) GROUP BY 1. On dev today that returns rows for exactly four columns: invoices.status (Issued, 4), bookings.status (Created, 128 — unless admitted), quotations.contract_status (NULL on 3 contract-type rows), users.status (Active, 4). Everything else is 0. Those four numbers are the backfillRows figures above.

attack.notes:
SCOPE. 19 attack probes + 2 controls, run as four verified real sign-ins against PostgREST on dev (oqermaidggvanahumjmj). Fixtures were created by SERVICE ROLE in a normal starting state and tagged E2E-STATE, so no probe tested its own ability to create the row.

HEADLINE: 14 distinct illegitimate jumps succeeded, across all four tables. ZERO probes were BLOCKED_LOUD. Nothing in the database raised on a status write, ever.

COMPACT TABLE (table | from | to | actor | verdict):
invoices | draft | posted (approval_status=pending_approval) | treasury | BREACH  <- G4, measured
invoices | draft | posted | bd | BLOCKED_SILENT (actor-level)
invoices | pending_approval | approved (approval_status) | treasury | BREACH
invoices | pending_approval | approved | bd | BLOCKED_SILENT (actor-level)
invoices | posted | draft | treasury | BREACH
invoices | draft | paid | treasury | BREACH
collections | pending | credited | treasury | BREACH
collections | posted | pending | treasury | BREACH
collections | posted | pending | bd | BLOCKED_SILENT (actor-level)
collections | posted | refunded | ops | BLOCKED_SILENT (dial: team vs created_by)
bookings | Created | Completed | bd | BREACH
bookings | Completed | Created | ops | BREACH
bookings | unbilled | billed (billing_status) | ops | BREACH
bookings | Cancelled | Ongoing | ops | BREACH
bookings | Cancelled | Ongoing | treasury | BLOCKED_SILENT (actor-level)
quotations | Draft | Accepted by Client | bd | BREACH
quotations | Draft | Converted to Project | bd | BREACH
quotations | Rejected by Client | Accepted by Client | pricingMgr | BREACH
quotations | Converted to Project | Draft | pricingMgr | BREACH

THE FIVE BLOCKED_SILENT RESULTS ARE NOT GUARDS. Every one is the actor failing to reach the row at all, and I proved it rather than assuming it:
  - BD on invoices: the control write to invoices.customer_name on a row SHE created was also BLOCKED_SILENT -> no invoices UPDATE authority whatsoever.
  - Treasury on bookings: the control write to bookings.name was also BLOCKED_SILENT -> no bookings UPDATE authority.
  - Ops on collections: her collections dial is 'team' and the fixture's created_by is the BD user, so the row falls outside USING. The identical jump landed for Treasury.
  - The Cancelled->Ongoing pair is the cleanest demonstration: BLOCKED_SILENT for Treasury, BREACH for Ops on an identical fixture. The state is not defended; only some actors can reach it.
So the correct before-picture is: on these four tables, if you can UPDATE the row at all, you can write any status string into it, from any state, in any direction. There is no from-state, no ordering, no approval gate, and no actor-vs-state pairing anywhere in the database.

SPECIFIC THINGS WORTH FLIPPING INTO EXPECTATIONS:
  1. G4 CONFIRMED, and it is worse than recorded. The finding says an unapproved invoice can be posted. It can also be APPROVED by a raw column write — Treasury moved approval_status pending_approval -> approved directly, so approve_invoice()'s SECURITY DEFINER approver check is one of two doors and the other one is unlocked. The client-side fallback noted by the survey (`(viewInvoice as any).approval_status ?? "approved"`) means a row with a NULL approval_status is also treated as approved by the finalize gate. Three bypasses of one approval, all live.
  2. invoices 'paid' is reachable and is a data-integrity hole, not just a vocabulary one: nothing writes 'paid', but useReceivablesAgingReport.ts:77 filters `.neq('status','paid')`. Writing it hides the invoice from the aging report permanently.
  3. bookings.billing_status is the ONLY status column in the survey with a CHECK constraint, and the constraint bought nothing. 'billed' is in the allowed vocabulary, so an Ops TL declared a booking billed with zero invoices against it. A vocabulary CHECK is not a transition guard; do not let its presence read as coverage.
  4. quotations contradicts finding E8 ("Only Pricing converts an accepted quote — BY DESIGN"). A BD staffer wrote 'Converted to Project' onto a Draft quote directly. E8 is a UI fact, not a system fact, and should be re-labelled.
  5. Un-converting a quotation (Converted to Project -> Draft) leaves the created project untouched. The reverse cascade at QuotationFileView.tsx:626 lives in the client, so the raw write desynchronises quotation and project.

HARNESS DISCIPLINE APPLIED: every probe asserted a value the row did not already hold and no probe ran from === to (K2); every verdict was read back with SERVICE-ROLE eyes rather than inferred from the absence of a PostgREST error (K1); all four sign-ins were verified to the point of resolving a users row from auth_id before any probe ran, and the run was set to abort on any failure (K3). No UNANSWERABLE results — every fixture was confirmed to be in its declared from-state before the attempt.

CLEANUP: all fixtures deleted in both passes, verified twice — once by the scripts re-selecting their own id lists (leftovers: none), and once independently via SQL sweeping projects/bookings/quotations/invoices/collections/billing_line_items for the E2E-STATE tag and the fixture number prefixes. All six counts are 0. Probe scripts were run from the repo root (for node_modules resolution) and then removed from the repo; they live at C:\Users\Marcus\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Marcus-Documents-Neuron-Development-NeuronosPrototype\624d4784-bab2-44dd-ac10-0eefaab0b776\scratchpad\state-probe.mjs and state-probe2.mjs. Nothing was written to prod; no supabase-prod tool was called.

NOT DETERMINED: I did not probe the remaining 8 live status columns (projects.status, quotations.contract_status, billing_line_items, customers, users.status, tasks) — out of the requested top-4 scope. The survey's claim that any authenticated user can write their own users.status is untested here and should not be counted as verified.
